chunks: From him, from Ibn Faddal, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Verily Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'The stingy one is the one who is stingy with the greeting (salam).'

key_terms.السَّلَام: The Islamic greeting of peace (al-salam) — 'Peace be upon you' (as-salamu alaykum)
key_terms.الْبَخِيل: The stingy/miserly one (al-bakhil) — one who withholds what they should give
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: A divine epithet meaning 'Mighty and Majestic', used exclusively for God
key_terms.يَبْخَل: To be stingy, to withhold miserly — same root as al-bakhil

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about the stingy person and the greeting of salam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) transmitted a divine saying (hadith qudsi) in which Allah Himself defines true stinginess not as withholding material wealth, but as withholding the greeting of salam. This reframes the concept of bukhl (miserliness) as applying to social and spiritual generosity, not merely financial. In the early Muslim community, initiating and exchanging the greeting of peace was considered a fundamental social obligation and a sign of brotherhood, making its withholding a form of spiritual and communal meanness.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Muawiya Bin Wahab,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said: “The stingy one, is the one who is stingy with the greeting (السَّلَامُ)’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ibn Faddal from Mu’awiyah ibn Wahab from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, ‘Really stingy is one who is stingy in offering the greeting of peace.’”
